subject: app-rdef
title: APP.RDEF. -----STF. ------SOC.RT.
description: Diagram in CMOA(II)-8 (Creative Music Outside of America, Level One — France/Italy/Northern Europe/Japan), first of two on book p250. (C)APP-RDEF (the concept of applied redefinitions) is crossed simultaneously with STF (source transfer) AND SOC-RT (social reality) — the unusual dual-partner formation indicating Braxton holds three concepts in tension. STF sits at the upper-center between subject and the second partner. SOC-RT anchors the upper-right. ALT-F (alternative functionalism) branches from the STF–SOC-RT stretch and carries AFTF (affinity transfer) at the lower-center, with PROJ-CONT (projectional continuance) hanging from AFTF, and CRTF-D (cross-transfer definitions) on the right, from which PR-TRS hangs at the lower-right. A *dashed* line from the main line below the subject runs down to LANG-DY (language dynamics) — a dotted line that, in Braxton's legend, 'amplifies some aspect of the main concept it is connected to' — and (R)POST (the reality of postulation) hangs from LANG-DY at the lower-left. Structural argument: applied-redefinitions-as-concept simultaneously crossed with source-transfer and social-reality branches through alternative-functionalism as central lower hub. The dual-partner formation is the structural claim that European reception of black creative music functioned via two simultaneous partners — source-transfer (the cultural transmission mechanism) and social-reality (the lived European condition).
